item.title: 米コア資本財受注、8月は1.6％増と予想上回る ＡＩ投資が下支え
item.description: [ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] - 米商務省が２５日発表した８月の耐久財受注は、民間設備投資の先行指標とされるコア資本...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米コア資本財受注、8月は1.6％増と予想上回る　ＡＩ投資が下支え 9/25 22:40 配信

米カリフォルニア州バレンシアのパシフィック・ロック工場で錠前を製造する従業員。２０２５年１２月撮影。REUTERS/Aude Guerrucci

[ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - 米商務省が２５日発表した８月の耐久財受注は、民間設備投資の先行指標とされるコア資本財（非国防資本財から航空機を除く）の受注が前月比１．６％増加した。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想（０．５％増）を上回る伸びとなり、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連インフラの構築を背景に、企業の設備投資が今四半期も堅調に拡大していることを示唆した。

７月は０．６％増と、速報値の変わらずから上方改定された。

８月は前年同月比では１０．６％増加した。

項目別の受注は、電気機器・家電・部品が１．１％増と伸びを主導した。コンピューター・関連製品は１．５％急増し、前年同月比では２０．１％増となった。通信機器は０．３％増、前年同月比では３５．８％急増した。

機械は１．１％、一次金属は１．２％それぞれ増加。一方、金属加工品は１．３％減少した。

自動車・部品は０．６％減。民間航空機は４．３％減となった。米航空機大手ボーイングのウェブサイトによると、８月の航空機受注数は１５機。７月は３８機だった。

非国防資本財の受注は１．２％増加した。

耐久財受注全体は７月の０．９％増から８月は横ばいとなった。輸送機器の受注が０．６％減少したことが重しとなった。耐久財受注はトースターから航空機まで３年以上使われるモノを指す。

８月のコア資本財の出荷は０．６％増。７月は１．４％増だった。

非国防資本財の出荷は１．３％減となった。

企業の設備投資は、ＡＩ関連の積極的な投資に支えられ２四半期連続で２桁の伸びを記録しており、製造業および経済全体を下支えしている。ただエコノミストらは、原油価格や金利、米長期債利回りの上昇を背景に、特にＡＩと関連の薄い分野の製造業が減速する可能性があると警鐘を鳴らしている。

ＦＷＤＢＯＮＤＳのチーフエコノミスト、クリストファー・ラプキー氏は「ＡＩ投資ブームは本物であり、経済全体をけん引している」と指摘。その上で「唯一のリスクは、いずれ全ての設備投資とデータセンターの建設が完了し、このＡＩバブルが膨張し切った後の成長要因が不透明であることだ。投資支出は成長の加速要因と見なされているが、いずれ終わりは必ず来る」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＩＴサービス企業、生成ＡＩ追い風に株価上昇か コラム：ＡＩ投資を「黄金」に変えたマイクロソフト、アルファベットは羨望か コラム：米アップル、ＥＶ断念でもＡＩによる収益化期待揺るがず コラム：ＡＩで相互依存強める新興企業と巨大ＩＴ コラム：ＡＩ企業の膨らむコスト負担、高品質データで争奪戦 最終更新: 9/26(土) 0:18 ロイター

item.title: TV networks resume covering White House as press access fight continues
item.description: US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump’s White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico.
item.dc:creator: Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: US television networks resumed coverage of President Donald Trump ’s White House events on Friday, providing the first live pool access for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit, as a legal battle continues over restrictions on CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Trump last week banned the three outlets from the White House, before a judge ordered the administration to [USN:L1N45G0ZE TEXT:"restore their access"]. The White House television press pool aired video of Xi's arrival at the White House for tea on the final day of the Chinese leader's visit, as well as the two leaders' [USN:L8N45G1YG TEXT:"tour of the National Archives"], which houses the US Constitution. CNN, ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC share the costs of covering the president and rotate coverage, providing pool footage to other outlets. The other networks' refusal to set up cameras in solidarity meant there was no pool coverage of the first two days of Xi's visit. CNN on Friday evening said it had been barred from traveling with Trump on Air Force One for a weekend trip to Tennessee. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters. Trump has long relied on the media to shape his public image and advance his agenda, even as he regularly casts news organizations as political adversaries. Since returning to office last year, his administration has taken an aggressive stance against major news outlets, including limiting access to the Oval Office and other restricted spaces. As pool coverage resumed for Xi's arrival at the White House on Friday, Trump declined to answer questions from reporters on China and Iran, his media ban and a controversial new taxpayer-funded TV ad that promotes his presidency. He later thanked reporters. "We appreciate the fair coverage. It's been very fair. We appreciate it," Trump later told reporters alongside Xi. The White House did not respond to a request for comment about the restored press access. UNPRECEDENTED CAMPAIGN [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"Trump banned the three news outlets"] from the White House complex over coverage he asserted was false or negative. Their access was reinstated on Thursday, after a federal judge deemed [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"the ban"] likely unconstitutional and ordered their access to be immediately restored. CNN, MS NOW and Politico sued Trump and other members of his administration, saying the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press, as well as their due process rights. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations, including Reuters, later filed a legal brief supporting the action. Despite the temporary ruling restoring access, the court has not yet resolved the main challenge to the ban, based on the First Amendment of the US Constitution that protects the right to free speech and a free press. The news outlets now have until September 28 to ask the judge to keep their access in place while the case moves forward. Even if the outlets won a permanent injunction against the ban, [USN:L1N45G0ZE TEXT:"Trump could still pursue his case"] in federal court. Trump has waged an unprecedented campaign against the media since returning to office last year, launching personal attacks on journalists, denying access to some outlets and suing news organizations, as well as calling on the Federal Communications Commission to strip broadcast stations of their licenses. FRIENDLIEST PRESS CORPS On Thursday, Trump made a joke to photographers in the Oval Office about China -- which imposes strict censorship across its media -- having the friendliest press corps, as he welcomed Xi to the White House. While the White House on Thursday told the court it had reinstated CNN, MS NOW and Politico's access, CNN and MS NOW later said some of their journalists were denied access to cover Xi's arrival for the White House state dinner, according to the Washington Post. A lawyer for the three outlets in court this week warned that the White House could again try to revoke the outlets' White House access as the current litigation continues. David Ellison, CEO of Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) , which is seeking to merge with CNN-parent Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD.O) , attended the [USN:L6N45G1DV TEXT:"Trump-Xi state dinner"] Thursday night. Critics have raised concerns about Paramount-owned CBS News tailoring coverage to favor Trump, although Ellison has promised to create an [USN:L4N45E0EO TEXT:"editorial independence board"] for both CBS and CNN as part of the deal.

item.description: [ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２５日、中国の習近平国家主席と「非常に実りある会談」を行ったとし、「素晴らしいことが起きるだろう」と自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」に投稿した。ただ、詳細については明らかにしなかった。

トランプ氏は２４日、習氏とホワイトハウスで会談。豪華な国賓待遇で習氏を迎え、儀礼的な演出は盛大だったものの具体的な成果は乏しく、人工知能（ＡＩ）、貿易、台湾、イラン情勢といった懸案事項について具体的な進展は確認されなかった。

item.title: 円が対ドルで3週ぶり大幅高、156円94銭－日米財務相が円安巡り協議
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ニューヨーク時間25日の外国為替市場で、円がドルに対して上げ幅を拡大した。日米財務相が同日に電話会談を行い、円の過小評価は問題だとの認識を再確認したと、日本の財務省が発表した。

円は対ドルで一時、ニューヨーク前日比1.2%高の1ドル＝156円94銭を付けた。9月7日以来、約3週間ぶりの大幅な上昇率となった。円は他の主要10通貨全てに対して上昇している。

発表資料によれば、片山さつき財務相とベッセント米財務長官は金融市場の動向などに関して意見を交換し、日米間の協力を一段と強化することで一致した。

円はそれ以前、片山氏が25日の会見で、日米首脳会談では「トランプ米大統領から円安への懸念が示された」と述べたことなどを受けて、既に上昇していた。

高市早苗首相も、一般論として「円の過小評価は問題である」とトランプ氏に首脳会談で伝えたと記者団に述べた。

ノムラ・インターナショナルの通貨ストラテジスト、宮入祐輔氏は、日米首脳会談後、政府高官から立て続けに出てきた発言を見ると「円安是正に向けた米国からの圧力は強いと感じる」と指摘。

「1ドル＝160円を超えてのドル・円上昇を期待していた一部の市場参加者の意欲を大きくそぐものとなり、それが、この日の円ショートカバーにつながった」との見解を示した。

ベッセント氏はまた、「日本の強固な経済ファンダメンタルズを反映した強い円が望ましい」との認識について片山氏と協議したと、SNSの投稿で明らかにした。

これについて宮入氏は、金融政策に関して、トランプ大統領からではないにせよ、引き続きベッセント氏から注文が入った可能性を指摘した。高市首相は25日、日米首脳会談では「金融政策、財政政策に関する議論はなかった」と記者団に語っていた。

宮入氏は「今後のドル・円相場は引き続き155－160円の大きなレンジの中で推移する」と予想し、「介入に関しては160円を超える円安になってからとみている」と述べた。

STOCKHOLM, Sept 25 : An expected European Union vote on allowing Tesla's supervised Full Self-Driving system across the bloc has been delayed from October, with the next apparent opportunity for a decision not before December, according to an agenda published on the EU's website. • Dutch regulator RDW approved the system in April, with Belgium and a handful of other countries following suit • RDW is also proposing that the software be approved across the bloc • Tesla said on September 1 in a post on X that an EU-wide vote could potentially happen on October 6

• However, the agenda for an October 6 meeting of the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV), which brings together representatives of EU member states and the European Commission, lists only a "continuation of discussions" on the Dutch request for an Article 39 authorisation, with 25 minutes allocated to the discussion • RDW told Reuters it would not speculate on the discussion, the vote or any potential outcome. • Tesla did not respond to a request for comment. In response to a post on X about the delayed vote, CEO Elon Musk wrote: "sigh" • The committee has already discussed Tesla's request at two previous meetings. The next scheduled TCMV meeting after October is in December, making that the earliest apparent opportunity for a vote based on the current agenda • An EU-wide rollout requires support by a "qualified majority" of 15 of the EU's 27 member states, representing 65 per cent of the bloc's population • Several EU countries, including Sweden, have expressed concerns about FSD exceeding speed limits, while countries that approved it say drivers remain responsible for complying with traffic laws • The same committee approved Ford's BlueCruise driver assistance system March 2024, with Germany as its sponsor • Tesla has called FSD approval key to boosting sales in Europe, where it is seeking to regain market share amid growing competition from Chinese electric-vehicle makers

Can AI produce para-athletes? Finalists from AP, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Odisha are among young innovators

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is a global initiative where students use technology to solve community challenges.

Sakshi Mehra

25 September, 2026 06:41 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File Photo | Kim Hong-Ji | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: Eight young innovators from Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Odisha have reached the Top 20 of the Samsung Solve for Tomorrow 2026 competition. They bring five technology-based ideas aimed at improving para-sports, athlete performance, swimming safety and exercise support for people with Parkinson’s disease.

Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is an innovation competition where students use STEM to solve community challenges. In its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

The eight innovators — Pasupuleti Ruthvik, Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla, Vatala Harika, Ritesh Routray, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, Jena R and Chriswin William D — are part of a national Top 20 cohort representing 18 cities across 12 states.

Show Full Article

More than half of the finalists come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, Samsung said. The Top 20 teams are now receiving mentorship and support to develop prototypes. Four winning teams will collectively receive Rs 2 crore in grants and incubation support from FITT-IIT Delhi.

Making swimming safer for visually impaired athletes Two of the five projects focus on challenges faced by visually impaired swimmers.

Pasupuleti Ruthvik, 21, from Chittoor developed Untethered, a wearable sensor system designed to alert swimmers when they are approaching the end of a pool lane.

For visually impaired swimmers, reaching the wall without a visual cue can be difficult and may result in head injuries. Ruthvik’s system provides real-time alerts, reducing dependence on manual cues from coaches and allowing swimmers to train more independently.

Kolla Venkata Siva Surya, 16, from Visakhapatnam, is working on a different challenge: maintaining direction inside the lane. His assistive trajectory system detects when a swimmer begins to move away from the intended path and provide real-time feedback, allowing the swimmer to correct their trajectory.

Also Read: Samsung turned first foldable iPhone launch into a roast. Apple fans are hitting back

Using AI to identify para-sport talent In Sundargarh, Vatala Harika, 21, and Ritesh Routray, 20, are using AI to identify para-athletes.

Their project, ParaSync, is an AI-based platform that assesses adaptive sporting techniques and identifies promising athletes. It also aims to connect them with professional coaching and competitive opportunities.

The project is based on the idea that sporting talent can emerge outside established sporting centres, where athletes may have fewer opportunities to access formal training and competition.

Wearables for safer exercise and training In Chennai, Manoj Kumar Kasinathan, 21, Jena R, 20, and Chriswin William D, 20, are developing Rogue, a wearable device aimed at supporting exercise for people with Parkinson’s disease.

In Hyderabad, 21-year-old Homanshika Reddy Pullagurla is developing Somatrace, an IoT-enabled wearable designed to monitor spinal load among precision-sport athletes.

The device tracks movement and physical load in real time, helping athletes understand the strain their bodies experience during training and how they respond to different movements.

The eight innovators took part in a prototyping programme with FITT-IIT Delhi that included an Innovation Bootcamp and online mentoring from Samsung experts.

The programme helped them understand users’ needs, develop prototypes, identify potential markets, and understand the impact and scalability of their ideas.

They also visited Samsung Design Delhi, Samsung R&D Institute India facilities in Noida, Delhi, and Bengaluru, and Samsung’s headquarters in Gurugram.

Now in its fifth edition in India, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow has four themes: AI Living for India, Health & Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech.

item.title: 中国はイラン支援せずと確約、トランプ氏が習主席に警告＝駐中国米大使
item.description:
Bo Erickson Susan Heavey Katharine Jackson Parisa Hafezi
［ワシントン ２５日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Bo Erickson　Susan Heavey　Katharine Jackson　Parisa Hafezi

［ワシントン　２５日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は２４日に行った中国の習近平国家主席との会談で、中国によるイラン支援は容認できないと明確に伝え、習主席は支援しないと確約した。米国のパデュー駐中国大使が２５日、明らかにした。

パデュー大使はＣＮＢＣのインタビューで「数週間前、イランへのいかなる支援も、直接か間接かを問わず、情報、部品、軍事装備のいずれであっても、全く容認できないと中国側に明確に伝えた」とした上で「トランプ大統領は昨日、あらためてこの点を非常に明確にした。このメッセージは継続的に発信している」と述べた。

ＦＯＸニュースの番組で、こうした状況は中国によるイラン支援停止を意味するのかとの質問に対し、「すでに動きが見られる。中国側は２４日、支援はしないとわれわれに保証した」と応じた。

パデュー氏はまたＣＮＢＣとのインタビューで、トランプ氏と習氏について「一定の信頼関係を築き始め、諸問題に取り組んでいる」と指摘。「非常に率直で開かれた会談だった」とし、両首脳が話すたびに、取り組んでいる懸案を巡り、より踏み込んだ意思疎通ができていると感じると語った。

トランプ大統領もこの日、習主席との会談でイラン情勢について協議したと確認。ただ、詳細は明らかにしなかった。

item.title: 米コア資本財の受注が予想を上回る－設備投資に依然勢い
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 8月の米耐久財受注統計（速報値）では、ビジネス機器の受注が予想を上回る伸びを示した。設備投資の勢いが続いていることが浮き彫りになった。

耐久財統計では、一次金属、機械、コンピューター、電気機器の受注が増加した。自動車と民間航空機の受注が減少し、輸送機器の受注は落ち込んだ。

今年はAI関連の支出にけん引され、設備投資と需要が堅調に推移している。企業による機器への設備投資は今年上期の国内総生産（GDP）の伸びに大きく寄与した。

この統計に先立って発表されたアトランタ連銀の予想モデル「GDPナウ」は、設備投資が第3四半期の成長率を1ポイント近く押し上げるとしていた。堅調な個人消費と合わせ、今回の耐久財統計は第3四半期も経済が力強く成長する下地が整っていることを示した。

航空機を含む非国防資本財の出荷は前月から1.3%減少した。これはGDP統計の設備投資項目に直接反映される。政府は取り消しが可能な受注ではなく、出荷データをGDPの算出に用いている。

ただ、今回の統計によるとコア資本財の出荷は0.6%増と、過去2カ月の大幅な伸びを下回った。

ブルームバーグ・エコノミクスのエコノミスト、エリザ・ウィンガー氏は「コア受注と出荷は、設備投資が第3四半期のGDP成長率に大きく寄与することを示唆している。AI関連支出に加え、より有利な税制環境が引き続き投資の勢いを支えている」と分析した。

エコノミストは基調的な設備投資を見極める上で、コア資本財の出荷を重視している。航空機や軍事関連は、受注から実際の出荷まで極めて長い時間がかかるためだ。

月ごとの変動が大きい民間航空機の受注は4.3%減少した。ボーイングは8月の受注が15機と、前月の38機から減少したと明らかにした。

item.title: Pope Leo warns that AI is creating 'paradise of machines'
item.description: Pope Leo says "there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment".
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Pope Leo warns that AI is creating 'paradise of machines'

Pope Leo says "there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment".

Pope Leo delivers a speech during a meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron and authorities, members of civil society and the diplomatic corps at the Elysee Palace in Paris as part of his four-day apostolic journey to France, on Sep 25, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/Pool)

25 Sep 2026 08:08PM (Updated: 25 Sep 2026 09:04PM)

FAST

PARIS: Pope Leo urged the world to reconsider the development of artificial intelligence , opening his four-day visit to France on Friday (Sep 25) with a fervent warning that AI could create a future where "a paradise of machines" takes control of the Earth. The first US pope, who has made sounding the alarm about the risks of AI a central part of his 16-month papacy, put the issue at the heart of his visit to France, the first by a pope in nearly 20 years. "If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a 'paradise of machines' invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment," he said, speaking under the gilded ceilings of the Elysee Palace. The pope also strongly reiterated the Church's pro-life teachings, criticising initiatives to allow assisted dying for those who have incurable illnesses, two months after French politicians approved such a measure.

"I am concerned … by those trends in society that risk turning science and technology into profit-driven ventures promoting genetic manipulation, surrogacy, the trade in human organs or the possibility of arranging one’s own death," he said. The pope, on a whirlwind three-city visit to France, will also seek to repair the Church's standing there after abuse scandals sparked nationwide shock, and is also expected to lay out a vision for the future of Europe in a speech on Monday.

Pope Leo XIV walks on a red carpet toward France's President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte Macron ahead of a meeting at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris on Sep 25, 2026, at the start of his four days visit to France. (Photo: Remo Casilli/POOL/AFP)

"MESSAGE OF PEACE" The pope was greeted at the Paris Orly airport, under a clear blue sky, by President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte, and by children who sang for him and asked for autographs. During his visit, he will travel to the famed Catholic shrine at Lourdes, in the southwest, and to Metz, on the German border. Pope Leo was due to lead a prayer service in Paris on Friday at the restored Notre-Dame cathedral, in the first visit by a pope since a devastating fire nearly destroyed the Gothic masterpiece in 2019. Telling reporters on the plane to Paris that he was coming to convey a message of peace, he added: "It is a message which at this time, as we all may know, is particularly important." People lining the streets Pope Leo was due to pass through on his way to the Elysee held up phones and waved flags and signs. "He brings a message of peace and hope that is very, very positive. His visit to France sends a wonderful signal to the country," a Catholic passer-by, Antoine Barxias-Casties, said in front of Notre-Dame cathedral on the eve of Pope Leo's visit. Next on the pope's agenda on Friday is a speech to staff at the headquarters of the UN culture and education body, UNESCO, which is facing budget shortfalls after US President Donald Trump withdrew from the agency in 2025. The first US pope attracted Trump's ire earlier this year after criticising the Iran war. Asked about Trump's attempt to bar CNN and several other outlets from the White House, Pope Leo, aboard the plane to Paris, reaffirmed his support for freedom of the press, saying all were welcome to cover his visit.

France's President Emmanuel Macron (L) welcomes Pope Leo XIV (R) ahead of a meeting at the Elysee Presidential Palace, in Paris on Sep 25, 2026 at the start of his four days visit to France. (Photo: Teresa Suarez/POOL/AFP)

SECULAR NATION France, a secular nation where the separation of church and state is enshrined in a 1905 law, has witnessed a steady decline in affiliation to the Catholic Church during the post-war era, mirroring a trend in other traditionally Catholic countries. Although the French Bishops' Conference points to an increase in baptisms of adults, a report published by the official statistics agency INSEE showed that only 25 per cent of French 18-to-49-year-olds identified as Catholic, compared with 43 per cent a decade earlier. Pope Leo's visit comes as Catholic leaders in France have been at odds with the government over the 2024 enshrining of a right to abortion in the French constitution, a world first, and the passage of the law legalising assisted dying for adults with incurable illnesses. POPE TO MEET ABUSE SURVIVORS Local Church leaders hope the pope's visit will repair the Church's standing after a crushing 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades. French bishops have since introduced compensation and safeguarding measures, but survivors have continued to press Church leaders to demonstrate accountability. "Leo bears the immense responsibility of 'declaring enough is enough'," Alain Esquerre, 66, a spokesperson for victims at the Notre-Dame de Bétharram Catholic institution, told Reuters. The pope will meet seven French victims of abuse by Catholic clergy on Sunday in Lourdes.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Sept 25 : Microsoft on Friday unveiled several new capabilities in its Copilot app, including a coding tool and an always-on AI agent, as the software giant seeks to transform its AI assistant into a one-stop shop for office workers. The company is also embedding its Office applications Word, Excel, and PowerPoint directly within Copilot, allowing users to work collaboratively on these apps without having to leave the AI tool. Shares of the Redmond, Washington-based company rose about 3 per cent in early trading. Microsoft is racing to expand Copilot beyond its chat-based roots to boost adoption as it competes with AI chatbots such as ChatGPT and Claude.

The Windows maker unveiled "Code" to let users build apps, dashboards and other software using natural language prompts. The tool, powered by the same technology as Microsoft's GitHub Copilot, will roll out to early-access customers at the end of the month, while 365 Premium and Pro subscribers can preview it later this year. Microsoft is also rolling out "Autopilot", a revamp of the "Scout" AI agent it unveiled in June, in a private preview at the end of the month. The so-called digital coworker agent will carry its own identity in the company directory and have specific permissions that users can control. "I think it's been very hard for many organizations to bring agents into the enterprise because of security, compliance and governance concerns," Annie Pearl, corporate vice president of Copilot Product, said in an interview. "So we've worked... to make sure that we were building this in a way that would really be able to be used in the enterprise." Microsoft also unveiled cost-management capabilities to allow employees to have direct insight into costs tied to their AI usage. The move comes at a time when enterprises are increasingly worried about rapid AI usage racking up unexpected costs.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Number of Sudanese fleeing to Chad surges 20-fold as aid runs dry, UN says
item.description: There has been a sharp increase in the number of people fleeing from Sudan to Chad to escape fighting and dire conditions, and aid funding is failing to keep up with needs, the United Nations refugee agency said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
item.content:encoded: There has been a sharp increase in the number of people fleeing from Sudan to Chad to [USN:L6N40Y0KB TEXT:"escape fighting"] and dire conditions, and aid funding is failing to keep up with needs, the United Nations refugee agency said on Friday. More than 400 people a day have been crossing into eastern Chad over the past week, a 20-fold increase from the numbers seen in recent months, UNHCR said. They were fleeing Sudan's Darfur, Kordofan and Blue Nile regions — which have all been hit by clashes between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in a more than three-year-old civil war. There were "people who tell us that they flee the conflict, they flee the aerial bombardments, they flee the drone attacks," Mamadou Dian Balde, UN Regional Refugee Coordinator for the Sudan Situation, told reporters in Geneva via video link from Nairobi. Only 18% of the $1.6 billion funding it needed this year had come in, UNHCR said. “It means less food. It means less capacity for people to be relocated to safer areas. It means less capacity to shelter themselves,” Dian Balde said. The agency warned of potential knock-on effects if Sudanese refugees’ basic needs are not met in Chad, saying its analysis shows many move on towards Europe after repeated failed attempts to find safety. The civil war has devastated wide swathes of Sudan, displacing up to 14 million people, ruining harvests and decimating the economy, according to UN estimates. Drought and other harsh conditions were also forcing people to move, UNHCR said. Almost 1 million refugees have crossed into Chad since the conflict began, more than 55,000 so far this year, according to UNHCR data. Aid groups like UNHCR face major funding shortfalls after the administration of US President Donald Trump and other donor countries cut billions of dollars in foreign assistance over the past year.

item.title: FRB、大手銀への監督強化巡る基準引き上げを計画－ロイター
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）は、大手銀行により厳格な監督を適用する際の基準となる資産額を引き上げる方向で検討を進めている。ロイター通信が匿名の関係者4人の話として報じた。

FRBは、銀行のバランスシートのストレステストや流動性、資本に関する規制の適用基準となる資産額の引き上げを検討している。関係者3人によれば、具体案は年内にも示される可能性がある。

2019年に設定された現行基準では、銀行の資産が1000億ドル（約15兆7600億円）を超えると規制が適用され、2500億ドルと7000億ドルを超えると追加の規制要件が課される。関係者がロイターに語ったところによると、最も低い基準は1500億ドルに、最も高い基準は1兆ドル近くに引き上げられる可能性がある。

基準の引き上げは、JPモルガン・チェースやシティグループなど米最大手銀行には影響しないものの、USバンコープやキャピタル・ワン・ファイナンシャルなどにとっては、最も厳しい規制の対象となるまでの余地が広がるとロイターは報じた。

item.title: India reserves third-party rights in Russia-EU CBAM trade dispute in WTO
item.description: India has reserved its third-party rights in a WTO dispute filed by Russia against the European Union over its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, allowing New Delhi to follow the proceedings ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / India reserves third-party rights in Russia-EU CBAM trade dispute in WTO

India reserves third-party rights in Russia-EU CBAM trade dispute in WTO India has reserved its third-party rights in a WTO dispute filed by Russia against the European Union over its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, allowing New Delhi to follow the proceedings

India, along with several other countries, has reserved its third-party rights to participate in proceedings related to a trade dispute filed by Russia against the European Union over its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Sep 25 2026 | 11:54 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India, along with several other countries, has reserved its third-party rights to participate in proceedings related to a trade dispute filed by Russia against the European Union over its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), as the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body has agreed to establish a panel to adjudicate the issue, an official said.   Argentina, Brazil, Canada, China, Chinese Taipei, Indonesia, Japan, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Malaysia, Norway, Paraguay, Singapore, Switzerland, Thailand, the UK and the US are other countries that have reserved their third-party rights in the dispute, the Geneva-based official said.   Russia has filed a dispute against the EU's CBAM package and alleged export subsidy under the EU scheme for trading greenhouse gas emission allowances.

The WTO Dispute Settlement Body, at its meeting in Geneva on Friday, agreed to set up a panel to adjudicate the matter, the official said.   Another official said becoming a third party in the case will help India follow the proceedings in the dispute. Also Read

PM Modi may visit Canada, Belgium in December for signing of trade pacts

"This is a constructive step for India as it will allow the country to see what is happening in the dispute. It can see the EU's as well as Russia's stand on the matter," the official added.   Third-party status would enable India to present its views on the WTO issues raised by Russia without becoming a principal party to the dispute.

The case is important for India because exporters of carbon-intensive products such as steel and aluminium face additional compliance requirements, including carbon costs and taxes, under the EU's CBAM regime.

Why the Trump-Xi summit just produced a truce, not a breakthrough

The Donald Trump-Xi Jinping Summit is best understood as the TRUCE, shaping a bipolar international system amid its multipolar pushbacks.

Swasti Rao

25 September, 2026 04:47 pm IST

2

T he pageantry in Washington was elaborate enough to make the Donald Trump-Xi Jinping summit look like a G2 truce. Trump personally received Xi at Joint Base Andrews. US aircraft such as B-2s and F-22s flew overhead, military bands marched, the White House rolled out a state dinner, Trump made Xi laugh and eventually discovered that the Chinese president shared his appreciation for one particular American asset: “ h e loves good granite”.

Strip away the granite, however, and a simpler question emerges: what kind of TRUCE did this truce actually achieve?

The answer can be decoded rather neatly by turning the word into an acronym.

Show Full Article

T for trade truce extended.

R for reciprocal leverage retained — Chinese rare earths versus American technology controls.

U for an unsettled Taiwan.

C for competition contained, not concluded.

E for engagement expanded, particularly on artificial intelligence (AI) , without much new institutional architecture.

TRUCE captures both change and continuity and shows the limits of G2. Washington and Beijing have bought themselves more stability, but they did not dismantle the instruments with which they compete or resolve the bottlenecks that engulf their strategic interests .

T: Trade truce, extended—not reinvented The conversation around the economic truce did not begin at the current summit.

Its immediate foundations were laid when Trump and Xi met in Busan, South Korea, on 30 October 2025, following months of tariff escalation. Under the arrangement implemented from 10 November in the same year , Washington suspended its heightened reciprocal tariffs on China for one year while retaining a 10 per cent reciprocal tariff. It also cut 10 percentage points from tariffs imposed over fentanyl flows.

China, meanwhile, reciprocated by suspending retaliatory tariffs and several non-tariff measures, easing restrictions involving rare earths and critical minerals, resuming purchases of American agricultural commodities and tightening controls on fentanyl precursors.

The Busan arrangement was due to expire on 10 November this year . As Xi arrived in Washington, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the truce would now continue until 10 January 2027.

This is where American political scientist Rush Doshi’s pre-summit checklist becomes quite useful to revisit. He argued that the duration of any extension would tell us something about the relationship itself. Beijing wanted a much longer period of stability while Washington preferred a shorter extension, partly because the US remained dissatisfied with Chinese compliance, particularly over critical-mineral supplies.

The outcome suggests quite convincingly that neither side wanted escalation, but Washington was unwilling to lock itself into détente in the guise of stability.

Also read: India-China reset has limits. Don’t mistake it for a boundary settlement — see Taksing

R: Reciprocal leverage retained Doshi’s more provocative argument concerned China’s changing leverage.

Beijing, he had argued before the summit, believes its ability to squeeze rare-earth supplies has altered Washington’s calculations. The present phase —  what he calls a “détente but not quite a détente” — suits the Chinese narrative that thinks time may increasingly favour it in the larger competition.

One need not accept that conclusion in entirety to see what has changed. Let me explain.

For decades, discussions of economic interdependence assumed that America’s advantages lay in technology and finance while China’s vulnerabilities lay in access to markets and advanced innovation. That part of the relationship is now considerably more reciprocal.

China has shown the geopolitical value of its dominance in critical-mineral processing. But Washington continues to wield formidable advantages through advanced semiconductor and technology controls.

During the current summit, neither has surrendered that leverage. Beijing’s official statement speaks of a “new joint arrangement” between the economic teams, but gives no dramatic new tariff concessions or the abandonment of Chinese critical-mineral leverage. It does not mention any major American relaxation of advanced-technology controls either.

Importantly, Beijing has released detailed official accounts of the summit in both Chinese and English. At the time of writing, there is no joint statement or a comparable detailed post-summit account from the White House. The Chinese version therefore provides the fullest available official account of the closed-door exchanges, but it cannot, by itself, establish what Washington agreed to.

The summit therefore did not conclude this coercive interdependence. It, however, established more political space for managing it.

That is a subtle but an important takeaway. US-China strategic stability increasingly depends not on resolving economic weaponisation, but on both realising how to manage the escalation around it.

Also read: Chinese commentary on Xi-Trump summit is a cross between flowers and daggers

U: Unsettled Taiwan Taiwan, once again, offers the clearest evidence of the limits of this new stability.

Xi asked Washington to accept what Beijing called their position of “opposing Taiwan independence.” The key phrase in Mandarin is fandui Taidu — literally, oppose Taiwan independence.

Washington’s established formulation has been close but not identical. It says that the US does not support Taiwan independence. Beijing would prefer something stronger but which Washington does not endorse.

Experts specifically said that semantics would be one of the tests worth watching.

Yet Beijing’s own statement records Xi making the demand without mentioning that the US accepted it.

Continued ambiguity on Taiwan, therefore, matters as much as subtle changes in Trump’s overall rhetoric to respect Beijing’s position. Once again, this deliberate word play remains a part of the broader management, not a conclusive position on their most dangerous fault line.

Trump’s uncertainty can itself have strategic consequences. But so far there is no evidence that Washington formally shifted to Beijing’s preferred formulation on Taiwan.

Also read: Trump’s Greenland deal changes little. His bullying can change US-Denmark ties

C: Competition contained — and Beijing wants a Naamkaran This is the most interesting part of the summit.

In May, Trump and Xi agreed in Beijing to pursue what both governments called a “constructive US-China relationship of strategic stability.” The White House itself used a closely matching phrase in its May fact sheet.

It is worth pausing here because “strategic stability” used by the US  traditionally carries a narrower, almost Cold War nuance — nuclear deterrence, escalation control and preventing catastrophic conflict between major powers.

Xi’s formulation is much broader. China’s official explanation describes constructive strategic stability as a relationship in which cooperation is the mainstay, competition remains within proper limits, differences are manageable, and peace can be expected. In other words, cooperate where possible, compete without losing control, manage what cannot be resolved, and prevent the rivalry from escalating to war.

The phrase, therefore, does not mean an absence of competition and seeks to define the acceptable boundaries of competition.

And Beijing clearly wants to institutionalise it. Xi’s statement said the two sides should now turn this vision “into action”. He wants engagement between ministries, economic officials, militaries and other institutions to thicken.

This is why I would distinguish constructive strategic stability, the actual agreed-upon phrase, from the looser idea of “comprehensive strategic stability”. Beijing’s ambition may indeed be comprehensive — extending beyond traditional military stability into economics, technology and political behaviour — but it is still not the terminology both governments officially adopted in May.

Once again, the difference in approach between Xi and Trump becomes telling.

Edgard Kagan, former US Ambassador to Malaysia , and now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), has also drawn attention to the importance of the relationship between the two leaders and the differences in how they approach the bilateral relationship. I would frame it as Trump personalises, but Xi institutionalises.

Trump speaks the language of friendship, deals and leader-to-leader chemistry and uses Trumpian pick-up lines to further his style of diplomacy. Xi speaks of frameworks, limits, departments, mechanisms and the formal relationship between two major powers.

Also read: How China sees US calls for AI slowdown. Its companies now get more room to catch up

E: Engagement expands—but does it ‘thicken’? AI may provide the best test here.

Before the summit, Bessent had already hailed emerging US-China AI discussions, and officials were exploring something more ambitious: communication mechanisms dealing with serious AI incidents and national-security risks.

Doshi, therefore, posed an excellent question before Xi arrived: would this dialogue become “thick” or remain “thin”?

If it indeed thickens — w ould agencies engage regularly? Would mechanisms survive political tensions? In a genuine emergency, would someone actually pick up the phone and make a call?

Washington Summit provided only a partial answer at best.

Xi proposed continuing AI dialogue, discussing both risks and benefits, preventing misuse and ensuring that artificial intelligence remains under human control. Trump, according to the Chinese statement, supported continued dialogue and cooperation.

But no genuine AI-safety regime emerged, and neither did any major bilateral mechanism come out. Trump has resisted imposing additional restraints on AI development, while Xi’s language repeatedly stresses human control.

So engagement has expanded enough for headlines, but its institutional architecture remains thin.

Also read: New India-US trade portal shows India is trying to liberalise and protect at the same time

More than spectacle, less than settlement This brings us back to Washington’s pageantry.

Reporting by Reuters described a meeting heavy on symbolism but light on breakthroughs across trade, Taiwan, AI and Iran.¹³ The Financial Times had anticipated pretty much the same logic before the talks, ie Xi’s central objective was to consolidate the more stable environment established since Busan and Beijing, rather than pin its success on headline-grabbers.¹⁴

There were continuities elsewhere too. One did not see any major new military crisis-management mechanism. Iran, Ukraine and the Korean Peninsula were discussed without producing breakthroughs. Beijing’s statement expectedly does not record a significant outcome on detainees or human rights.⁶

Yet calling the summit inconsequential because the deliverables were thin would miss its larger importance where due.

Trump and Xi appear to have moved from repeatedly asking whether their rivalry can be resolved to how a rivalry that cannot be resolved can be managed.

That is where constructive strategic stability and lack of unending breakthroughs become reassuring, even if with a hint of discomfort.

Uncomfortable, because the concept could also become a vehicle through which each tries to constrain the other’s behaviour. Seeking strategic stability cannot be indefinitely politically neutral.

Also read: The India-China reset will be tested in the Northeast

The bipolar ceiling above a multipolar world There is one reason why the Washington summit matters.

Writing in The Indian Express ahead of the summit, C Raja Mohan argued that multilateral institutions, however ambitious, operate within parameters set by great-power politics rather than independently determining the international order.

The Xi-Trump summit happened as leaders from across the world gathered around the United Nations, trying to assert their agency and space in the era of growing unpredictability.

At the granular level, the contemporary international system increasingly looks multipolar. Middle powers have become more active. New plurilaterals have proliferated — the latest being the Partners for Multilateralism that Canada floated with the EU, India, Brazil, Kenya, Australia and Barbados on board.

India, Europe, Japan, Australia and the Gulf states have been developing overlapping strategic partnerships. These middle-power initiatives promise issue-based cooperation outside traditional great-power blocs.

Yet the world’s most consequential strategic questions continue operating in an oddly bipolar world.

Whichever way the elusive G2 is defined, neither Washington nor Beijing can simply dictate outcomes to others. But they continue to shape an extraordinary portion of the international system’s grand strategic boundaries.

Therefore, the Washington truce is best understood as the TRUCE, shaping a bipolar international system amid its multipolar pushback.

Swasti Rao is a Consulting Editor (International and Strategic Affairs) at ThePrint. She tweets @swasrao. Views are personal.

item.title: Govt orders crackdown on nicotine pouches citing health concerns
item.description: India has directed states to crack down on the illegal sale of nicotine pouches, citing health risks and increased availability through online and offline channels.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / News / Govt orders crackdown on nicotine pouches citing health concerns

Govt orders crackdown on nicotine pouches citing health concerns India has directed states to crack down on the illegal sale of nicotine pouches, citing health risks and increased availability through online and offline channels.

Nicotine pouches have emerged as one of Big Tobacco's most important bets on a future beyond cigarettes | Representative Image

Reuters NEW DELHI, Sept 25 3 min read Last Updated : Sep 25 2026 | 11:38 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's government has ordered states to crack down on the sale of nicotine pouches, which it considers a major health risk, saying globally popular brands are being widely sold illegally in the country, a letter from the health ministry shows. Nicotine pouches have emerged as one of Big Tobacco's most important bets on a future beyond cigarettes, offering rapid growth, attractive margins and, for now, lighter regulation than many rival smoking alternatives. In India, where tobacco kills 1.35 million people a year, the government has banned e-cigarettes but approved certain nicotine replacements like patches and chewing gums. Nicotine pouches - small packets placed under the lip that contain nicotine but no tobacco - remain illegal and unapproved, with a government source saying they are often smuggled into India for sale online and through local tobacco stores.   A federal study in June called them "a largely unregulated public health concern", with wide consumption among people aged 18 to 40 of brands such as Philip Morris' Zyn and Swedish Smokeless Solutions' White Fox. Also Read

SC sets deadlines for ICU infrastructure upgrades, critical-care staff

Severe Covid-19 may 'wake up' dormant viruses in the body, study finds

Sun Pharma's Unloxcyt posts 50% response rate in skin cancer study

UK bans cigarette sales for future generations: Can India replicate?

Sweet binge triggers paralysis: What is hypokalemic periodic paralysis?

There is increased "availability of oral nicotine pouches through online and offline channels in the country ... Nicotine exposure is of particular concern among children," the health ministry wrote in a letter to all states on September 19, seen by Reuters. "Initiate appropriate enforcement action in accordance with the law, in the interest of public health and protection of children," it added. The directive cited provisions of India's drug law that allow for the search and seizure of such products and the prosecution of those selling them. The ministry did not respond to requests for comment. Philip Morris and Swedish Smokeless did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Philip Morris on its website says the company has zero tolerance towards illegal trade, while Swedish Smokeless urges users to only buy original products from authorised outlets. While the World Health Organization has said governments need to introduce more safeguards to protect people, especially youth, from nicotine pouch addiction, some agencies such as the U.S. Food and Drug Administration say smokers who switch completely to alternatives such as pouches, vapes and heated tobacco products may reduce their health risks. NO NEW APPROVALS In April, an Indian investigation found that Mumbai international airport's duty-free shops run by billionaire Gautam Adani's business group breached the law by selling nicotine pouches. Adani has denied wrongdoing, and an Indian court this week rejected the company's arguments that duty-free shops are immune from domestic laws. It also told the Adani Group it was free to make representations before the government to make a case for the pouches. However, the government believes "nicotine pouches are addictive, pose independent health risks and have not been established as effective smoking-cessation aids," according to minutes of the main federal drug panel's meeting published on September 16. The Drugs Technical Advisory Board "recommended that no new nicotine formulation be approved henceforth in public interest," it added.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: ウクライナ財政・国防支援、ＥＵ・ＩＭＦも重要性理解＝大統領
item.description: [キーウ ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[キーウ ２５日 ロイター] - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は２５日、欧州連合（ＥＵ）と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）が、ウクライナの財政赤字を補い、国防費を賄うための支援の重要性を理解していると述べた。

ゼレンスキー氏は、１０月と１１月に無人機（ドローン）を発注する必要があり、できなければ来年初めに困難な状況に直面すると語った。

メッセージアプリ「ワッツアップ」を通じた記者会見で「ウクライナだけでは対応できず、ウクライナ製のドローンやミサイルへの投資を増やす必要があることを誰もが理解している」と述べた。ＥＵのフォンデアライエン欧州委員長から前向きな回答を得たとも明らかにした。

ウクライナは国防費だけでなく、社会保障費や人道支援に関する支出も海外からの支援に頼っている。来年は５２０億ドルを超える国際的な資金支援が必要になると見込んでいる。

マルチェンコ財務相は記者団に対し、ウクライナ向け融資プログラムの第２次審査を行うＩＭＦ調査団が１１月に訪問する見通しだと述べた。それまでに来年の予算の財源確保に向けた計画を策定する必要があるとした。

item.title: TSX ends near flat for the week as financial shares rally
item.description: Canada's main stock index ended higher on Friday, led by gains for financial shares, as domestic bond yields pulled back from multi-year highs.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index ended higher on Friday, led by gains for financial shares, as domestic bond yields pulled back from multi-year highs. The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 94.43 points, or 0.3%, at 35,800.89, a day after posting its lowest closing level in eight days. For the week, the index was barely changed, dipping 0.02%. "Rising bond yields are a headwind for the market because it suggests there's expectations of higher interest rates and rate hikes," said Colin Cieszynski, chief market strategist at SIA Wealth Management. "So the decline in bond yields is short-term, at least, positive," Cieszynski said. "The headwinds fade a little bit and that's helped the markets pick up today." The Canadian 10-year yield eased 7.5 basis points to 3.923%, after touching its highest level since October 2023 at 4.011% during Thursday's session. Preliminary domestic data showed that [USN:S0N3ZU02D TEXT:"wholesale trade"] declined 1.5% in August from July. Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) added 1.1%, helped by gains for major banks. [USN:TUA8RPQ6L TEXT:"National Bank of Canada"] (NA.TO) announced plans to buy back up to 10 million shares. Its shares ended 1.4% higher. Shares of auto parts supplier Magna International (MG.TO) rose 4.7%, which helped lift consumer discretionary (.GSPTTCD) by 2.2%. Energy (.SPTTEN) was a drag, falling 0.8%, as [USN:L6N45H0YH TEXT:"U.S. crude oil futures"] settled 2.3% lower at $92.41 a barrel on mounting hopes for a truce between the US and Iran. Technology (.SPTTTK) was down 1.1%, with BlackBerry (BB.TO) shares falling 5.7%.

item.title: メッカ防衛協定、イラン参加も可能＝トルコ国会議長 - ロイター
item.description: メッカ防衛協定、イラン参加も可能＝トルコ国会議長 ロイター

item.title: メッカ防衛協定、イラン参加も可能＝トルコ国会議長
item.description: [アンカラ ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[アンカラ ２５日 ロイター] - トルコのクルトゥルムシュ国会議長は２５日、トルコ、サウジアラビア、パキスタンが合意した「メッカ共同防衛協定」について、イランも含む「イスラム世界のための」より広範な協定に発展する可能性があると述べた。

アンカラで記者団に「国際協定の発効には国会の承認が必要だ。現在行われている協定関連の会合は準備段階のものだ」と説明した。国会が１０月に休会明けを迎えることに触れ、「近く審議される見込みだ」と述べた。

協定がイランに対抗するものかとの質問に対し、特定の国を標的としたものではないとするトルコの立場を改めて示した。紛争やイスラエルの「敵対的政策」が続く中、地域諸国の安全確保を主眼に置いたものだと説明した。

「メッカ協定をイランに対抗する協定とは全く考えておらず、そうあってはならない。むしろイスラム世界のためのより広範な協定に発展することを望んでいる。イランも参加でき、他の地域諸国の参加によって協定が一層強固になることを期待している」と語った。

item.title: Russia Sanctions bill gives US President "new tool" with national security waivers, does not mean he deploys it tomorrow: Senior State Department official
item.description: The legislation has raised concerns, and the Ministry of External Affairs has said that India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people will continue to do so ...
item.content:encoded:
Russia Sanctions bill gives US President "new tool" with national security waivers, does not mean he deploys it tomorrow: Senior State Department official The legislation has raised concerns, and the Ministry of External Affairs has said that India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics. ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 23:15 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 23:15 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Russia Sanctions Bill has given President Donald Trump another tool in his toolkit but that doesn’t necessarily mean he will deploy it, a senior US State Department official has said, noting that it provides a huge national security waiver. The legislation has raised concerns, and the Ministry of External Affairs has said that India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics. MEA also said the issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors and its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side. The senior US State Department official said that while the legislation has been passed,  its practical application remains under careful evaluation. “On the Lindsey Graham (Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026), I think what people are not understanding is Congress gave the President another tool in his toolkit. That doesn’t mean necessarily that he’s going to implement that tomorrow, but what Congress gave the President is another ability to implement sanctions where necessary. I think the idea that it’s going to happen tomorrow, I can’t tell you that. But it’s another tool in his toolbox,” the official said. Addressing questions regarding potential diplomatic friction and whether New Delhi might seek exemptions, the official emphasised that the legislation includes broad flexibility for the executive branch to navigate national security priorities. “At the same time, they gave him a huge national security waiver, which you see in this legislation a lot. So we’ll have to wait and see in the coming days, but I think it’s, the way I would phrase it is that the President now has another tool. That does not necessarily mean he deploys it. And he has a broad national security waiver, and so we’ll see what that looks like in the coming days,” the official added. The official said that the President’s focus is on ending the Russia-Ukraine war. “It’s been something he campaigned on and something he’s been dedicated to from the beginning. We’re looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort, but I think you’ll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine also the President, there’s a scenario the President uses that as well.” External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week in New York and raised India’s crucial economic and strategic concerns regarding legislation targeting buyers of Russian energy. During the bilateral talks, Jaishankar raised concerns about the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA), a bill aimed at imposing steep tariffs of up to 100% on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas. Sharing an update in a post on X, Jaishankar highlighted the core issues discussed during their interaction."Good to meet @SecRubio of the US #UNHighLevelWeek," Jaishankar posted. "Reiterated India's interests and concerns with regard to SRIA. Also discussed the Gulf and Ukraine situations." Last Friday, President Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law, which empowers the executive branch to levy tariffs of up to 100 per cent on nations importing Russian oil and gas, encompassing major economies like India and China. The legislation pays tribute to the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who had initially championed a sanctions framework targeting purchasers of Russian petroleum with extreme tariff rates. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: A Lapel Pin Fuels Chinese Talk of a China-Russia-Iran Triangle
item.description: In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one …
item.dc:creator: Rudy Lu
item.content:encoded:
In China’s tightly managed political information environment, seemingly trivial interactions between senior officials can become material for close reading. Netizens and commentators scrutinize seconds-long clips — who smiles, who initiates a handshake, how firmly leaders grip hands or whether they appear unusually relaxed around one another — for clues about relationships that official readouts rarely reveal.

A brief encounter between the foreign ministers of China, Russia and Iran at the BRICS summit has become the latest example.

Video from the sidelines of the summit in New Delhi showed Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi chatting and laughing with his Russian and Iranian counterparts Sergei Lavrov and Abbas Araghchi. At one point, Wang reached toward a pin on Araghchi’s jacket, prompting the Iranian foreign minister to laugh.

Araghchi’s official Telegram channel later posted a close-up of the exchange , identifying the pin as an emblem depicting the map of Iran.

The moment quickly spread across Chinese social media, landing on the trending search list of Weibo, a Chinese social media platform often compared to X, under “Wang Yi helps the Iranian foreign minister straighten his pin” (#王毅帮伊朗外长整理胸针).

A wave of Chinese-language amplification followed.

Nationalist commentary account Rongping (戎评) described Iran as “holding the advantage” and in high spirits, with China and Russia sharing the mood.

“Such a personal and warm interaction between the Chinese and Iranian foreign ministers sends a strong signal to the outside world: China-Iran relations have long gone beyond a simple exchange of interests, and the two sides share a high degree of familiarity and trust,” it wrote.

Another online commentary said the seemingly insignificant gesture reflected a shift in the international balance of power that would make the White House “deeply uncomfortable.”

“U.S. pressure is pushing the three sides closer together,” it said. “Washington can continue to pressure the three countries separately, but it will find it increasingly difficult to stop them from exchanging resources, coordinating positions and jointly seeking alternatives.”

It said Beijing could keep channels open to Gulf Arab countries, and Moscow could draw on its close strategic ties with Tehran. Working through BRICS, the three could help Iran break its diplomatic isolation and avert a complete rupture with the United Arab Emirates and other Gulf states.

Those interpretations, however, largely reflect one strand of domestic online opinion that is sympathetic to Iran and distrustful of the United States. Beijing’s official posture has been more carefully calibrated, especially ahead of Xi Jinping’s scheduled Sept. 24 meeting with Trump in Washington.

Araghchi traveled to Beijing on Sep. 16 for talks with Wang Yi. The Chinese Foreign Ministry described Iran as a “comprehensive strategic partner” and said Beijing was prepared to help safeguard Tehran’s “legitimate rights and interests.”

But much of Wang’s message focused on containing the conflict. He urged Iran and the United States to exercise restraint and return to negotiations, backed dialogue between Tehran and Gulf Arab governments, called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and warned against the fighting spreading toward Yemen and the Red Sea.

China’s balancing role was also evident when Saudi Arabia asked Beijing to press Iran to rein in the Houthis, Reuters reported, citing three Iranian sources . China then privately urged Tehran to use its influence over the Yemeni group, whose advances threatened Saudi oil exports and shipping through the Red Sea — a vital route for Chinese trade.

PARIS, Sept 25 : Crypto exchange Bitget has stopped allowing customer withdrawals following the theft of crypto worth approximately $351.6 million in a hack, it said, adding all user funds were safe. Bitget had noticed "unauthorised transfers" from some of its wallets on Thursday and it "temporarily suspended" customer withdrawals, Gracy Chen, CEO of the Seychelles-based company, said in a statement posted on X. Chen said that all user funds were safe and that the loss was covered by Bitget's own funds. "Withdrawals remain temporarily suspended as a security precaution, not because of any shortfall in funds," Chen told Reuters in an emailed statement on Friday.

Bitget says it has more than 120 million users, making it one of the world's largest crypto exchanges. Crypto exchanges have for years been subject to hacks and thefts. Last year, crypto exchange Bybit had $1.5 billion stolen in a hack, which the FBI attributed to North Korean hackers.  North Korea routinely denies involvement in cyber hacking or crypto heists.  Authorities have said criminals can quickly move stolen cryptocurrency across borders, without using the mainstream financial system.

item.title: India-US trade deal 90% complete, to unleash another level of ties: US State Dept official
item.description: The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI.
item.content:encoded:
India-US trade deal 90% complete, to unleash another level of ties: US State Dept official The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI. ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 23:06 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 23:06 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The India-US trade deal is “90 per cent completed,” with just final details left to be worked out, a senior US State Department official told ANI. The State Department official termed the trade deal the “most sticking point” and which can potentially “unleash another level” of India-US relations. The official said, “I would say stay tuned, which we keep saying, but we are very close. It’s like a 90-per cent-plus there and just those final things being worked out, so I hope you’re going to see something very soon on that.  And that’s really going to just unleash another level of US-India relations, something that hasn’t really – we haven’t been able to get there in decades when it comes to trade. This has always been the most sticking point in the relationship.  So I think we’re very close and it’s going to be very, very exciting when we get there.” Meanwhile, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said India and the US have “done and dusted” the trade pact and will execute it once Washington gives India the right competitive advantage over its rivals in the American market. India and the US came up with an interim framework for the trade deal in February 2026, and the negotiations are ongoing to finalise the Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA). Speaking at the 13th Annual Forum 2026 India 3.0, the Commerce Minister said, “The nine agreements include the US, which is almost done and dusted. We have to find the right comparable competitive advantage over our competitors so that we can quickly execute the agreement.” Earlier, US-India Business Council (USIBC) President, Ambassador (ret.) Atul Keshap said that the US and India should intensify efforts to conclude a “historic” trade agreement that lowers trade barriers and minimises tariffs, providing greater certainty to the bilateral economic and strategic partnership, according to a statement by USIBC. Calling on both governments to intensify efforts to conclude a trade agreement, Keshap said unlocking reciprocal trade would build on the record investments made in 2026 and benefit businesses in both India and the US. (ANI)

ベイリー氏は25日、オックスフォードで行われたオックスフォード大学とニューヨーク連銀が共催したイベントのパネル討論に出席。英中銀は中東での紛争開始以降、政策金利を据え置いてきたが、エネルギー価格が高止まりする期間が長くなるほど、「そのスタンスを維持することは難しくなるだろう」と述べた。

item.title: Private corporate capex estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in FY27, investment momentum sustained: RBI Bulletin
item.description: Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, ...
item.content:encoded:
Private corporate capex estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in FY27, investment momentum sustained: RBI Bulletin Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, according to an article in the Reserve Bank of India's September Bulletin. ANI | Updated: 25-09-2026 22:51 IST | Created: 25-09-2026 22:51 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Capital expenditure by India's private corporate sector is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27 based on the pipeline of ongoing projects, indicating continued momentum in private investment, according to an article in the Reserve Bank of India's September Bulletin. “The phasing profile of the pipeline projects based on all channels of financing taken together, suggests that the envisaged capex is estimated at Rs 3.2 lakh crore in 2026-27, indicating sustained momentum in private investment,” the RBI said in its press release in the Bulletin. The estimate is based on projects financed through banks and financial institutions, external commercial borrowings (ECBs), and initial public offerings (IPOs). The Bulletin article said comparable capex from these funding channels stood at Rs 2.6 lakh crore in 2025-26. It added that complete information on projects that will be sanctioned during FY27 is not yet available, and therefore the outlook is based on the pipeline of projects sanctioned in earlier years. Private investment activity had strengthened in the previous financial year as well. The total cost of projects sanctioned by banks and financial institutions increased to a record Rs 4.4 lakh crore in 2025-26 from Rs 3.7 lakh crore in the previous year. “Private corporate investment intentions remained resilient during 2025-26 despite a challenging global environment marked by heightened geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty, and volatile financial markets,” the Bulletin article said. Infrastructure remained the biggest destination for investment, accounting for 54.2 per cent of the total cost of projects sanctioned by banks and financial institutions in 2025-26. The power sector was the major contributor, followed by roads and bridges. The bulletin said, “Infrastructure continued to dominate the investment landscape, led by the power sector.” It also noted that greenfield projects accounted for 89.2 per cent of the total cost of projects reported by banks and financial institutions during FY26, pointing to capacity expansion by private companies. “Looking ahead, the investment outlook is expected to remain healthy, although heightened global uncertainties are likely to temper the investment sentiment,” the Bulletin article said. The RBI clarified that views expressed in Bulletin articles are those of the authors and do not represent the views of the Reserve Bank of India. (ANI)

item.title: EU, IMF understand need to help Ukraine finance budget gap, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that the European Union and the International Monetary Fund understood the importance of helping Kyiv finance its budget deficit and defence spending.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that the European Union and the International Monetary Fund understood the importance of helping Kyiv finance its budget deficit and defence spending. Ukraine is seeking an additional $27 billion from partners this year for defence, saying the cost of the war has risen as Ukraine and Russia intensify long-range drone and missile attacks on each other's military and economic assets, while continuing to fight along a 1,200-km (745-mile) front line. Kyiv has asked to bring forward part of a loan from the European Union. Zelenskiy said Ukraine needed to order drones in October and November or it would face challenges at the start of next year. "Everyone understands that Ukraine cannot be alone, and that more investment is needed in Ukrainian-made drones and missiles," he told reporters in a WhatsApp briefing, adding that he had received a positive response from European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Aside from defence, Ukraine also relies on foreign help to finance its social and humanitarian spending. It expects to need [USN:L1N4580AK TEXT:"more than $52 billion"] in international financial aid next year. Finance Minister Sergii Marchenko told reporters that an IMF mission for a second review of Ukraine's financing programme was expected in November and that Kyiv needed to have a plan in place by then for how to fund next year's budget. One of Ukraine's largest companies, the Fozzy Group, said in a post on Facebook that damage caused by Russian attacks was obliging it to lay off staff at its network of shops and in its offices. It gave no specific figures, but said it was still hiring staff to work in facilities restored after attacks. "From August 1 to September 25 alone, the Russians destroyed and damaged more than 20 of our facilities — distribution centers, supermarkets, and production capacities," it said. "We lost part of our infrastructure and inventory and keeping things running smoothly has become much harder and more expensive."

item.title: 英企業、ウクライナ戦場データ活用へ ドローン向けＡＩ開発巡り
item.description:

• バーナム英首相とゼレンスキー・ウクライナ大統領との間で結ばれた合意により、ウクライナ国内で無人航空機システムによって収集された画像や動画のデータベースへのアクセスが許可されることとなった。このデータベースには、戦車、大口径の火砲 、防空システム、歩兵、空中目標など、６００万件以上の物体検知データが含まれている。

• ストリーティング英国防相は声明で「実戦データへのこの世界初のアクセスにより、英国企業は防衛イノベーションの最前線を押し広げ続け、敵を抑止し、国内の安全を確保するとともに、ウクライナをさらに強化することができるだろう」と述べた。

Nupur Anand Pete Schroeder Saeed Azhar
[ニューヨーク／ワシントン ２５日 ロイ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米ＦＲＢ、大手銀行の監督巡り資産基準緩和を計画＝関係筋 9/25 19:10 配信

2015年12月撮影　REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque/File Photo

Nupur Anand　Pete Schroeder　Saeed Azhar

[ニューヨーク／ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が、大手銀行に対する厳格な監督を発動する資産規模の基準を引き上げる計画を進めていることが、関係者４人の話で明らかになった。実現すれば、一部の銀行はコストのかかる追加規制を回避できるようになり、業界再編を促す可能性がある。

関係者によると、ＦＲＢは近く、健全性審査（ストレステスト）や流動性、資本などに関するより厳格なルールが適用される資産規模の基準について、インフレと経済成長を反映するよう見直しを提案する見通し。関係者のうち３人は、ＦＲＢが年内にも変更案を提示するとみている。

現行の規則では、銀行の資産規模が１０００億ドルに達すると規制が厳しくなり、２５００億ドル、さらに７０００億ドルで段階的に強化される。銀行側は、２０１９年に設定されたこうした基準が経済実態に即しておらず、実際のリスクに見合わない厳しい監督を強いられていると主張している。

関係者によると、ＦＲＢは最上位の基準を１兆ドル近くに引き上げるほか、より低い基準で適用される規制の一部について、適用基準を１５００億ドル近くに引き上げる計画だ。

ＦＲＢ報道官はコメントを控えた。

item.title: Trump continues voter data push despite repeated setbacks
item.description: President Donald Trump is pressing forward with his administration's pursuit of sensitive voter data despite repeated losses in court, seeking to identify noncitizens illegally registered to vote even though there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud.
item.dc:creator: Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump is pressing forward with his administration's pursuit of sensitive voter data despite repeated losses in court, seeking to identify noncitizens illegally registered to vote even though there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud. Justice Department lawyers, responding to a legal challenge to a key element of Trump's plans, urged a federal judge in Maryland on Friday not to block the Department of Homeland Security from creating lists of US citizens who are eligible to vote. Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterms . US District Judge Paula Xinis did not immediately rule on a request by privacy advocates, who asked that she block implementation of an [USN:S0N3ZK0A9 TEXT:"executive order"] Trump signed in March, but she instructed the Justice Department to give her at least 30 days' notice before distributing the lists. Trump's order directed DHS to create the citizen lists using data housed throughout the federal government and share them with state election officials. Under the order, state officials could face criminal prosecution if ineligible people are found to have voted in their states. The federal government has never previously compiled any such lists. The US Constitution assigns the administration of federal elections to individual states. The plaintiffs argue that the DHS plan to create the lists would collect information on American citizens from other federal government entities including the Social Security Administration in ways that violate privacy laws. Trump for years has made false claims about widespread voting fraud in the US including in his loss to Democrat Joe Biden in the 2020 presidential election. Trump, who has said he is acting to protect the integrity of US elections, also has asserted that states are not doing enough to remove noncitizens and dead people from their voter rolls. Critics have said that Trump's current drive is aimed at disenfranchising eligible Democratic-leaning voters. They note that a federal immigration database known as SAVE, which is one of the sources that Trump's executive order directs DHS to consult in building its lists of eligible voters, has mistakenly flagged as noncitizens some Americans who are naturalized US citizens and properly registered to vote. Several Republican-led states already have checked their voter rolls against SAVE. 25 LOSSES IN COURT Most of the Trump administration's efforts to collect voter data have not succeeded. Trump's proposed SAVE America Act, legislation that would require states to check their voter lists against the SAVE database, failed in the Republican-controlled Senate. The Justice Department has [USN:L6N44118V TEXT:"lost 25 lawsuits"] seeking to compel states to hand over their complete voter rolls, including sensitive information such as partial Social Security numbers used to identify people. And the US Supreme Court this month [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"declined to allow"] his push to tighten mail-in voting, which would have required states to submit lists of eligible voters to the US Postal Service. In a [USN:L1N45H0IZ TEXT:"victory for Trump"], however, the Supreme Court on Friday allowed the administration to use a revamped version of SAVE to check voter eligibility, after a lower court blocked it in a separate case. The justices acknowledged, however, that it may be too close to the election for officials to conduct large-scale reviews of their voter rolls to remove ineligible voters. In a July speech, Trump said without providing evidence that hundreds of thousands of noncitizens and dead people were listed as active on voter rolls, and that he directed DHS to tell states to remove them. "We have very important elections coming up. We want those elections to be honest," Trump said. White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement: "Despite extreme Democrats and the media claiming it never happens, the evidence of noncitizens registering and voting in our elections continues to pile up." 'MASS DISENFRANCHISEMENT' Democrats and voting rights advocates say the administration's focus on obtaining voter data and checking for noncitizens is driven by a desire to impose obstacles on Democratic-leaning voters, rather than a genuine concern about election security. "You can't do mass disenfranchisement without a voter file," said voting rights lawyer Marc Elias, whose firm frequently represents the Democratic Party in court. John Hill, a lawyer at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, which is representing the plaintiffs challenging the DHS plans on Friday, said Trump's threat of prosecution of state officials implied that his administration would try to coerce states to use DHS's citizenship lists to purge voters. At Friday's hearing, Justice Department lawyer Joshua Schopf told the judge that the lawsuit is premature because DHS has not yet activated the online portal through which it intends to share voter data with the states. Schopf did not say when the portal would go live or rule out activating it before the election. GLITCHES AND CLERICAL ERRORS A Reuters review published on Wednesday found that software glitches and [USN:L1N45F0H5 TEXT:"clerical errors"] in a dozen US states run by both Democrats and Republicans may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to the nation's voter rolls since 2000. Reuters was not able to determine how many of the noncitizens voted. Experts said the number was too small to affect elections. In an example that Trump's White House has cited to argue that Democrats are wrong to suggest noncitizen voting is not a concern, New Jersey said in July that a technology glitch added 6,600 noncitizens to voter rolls in 2023 and 2024. The state said fewer than 400 of them actually voted, and that there was no evidence that the results of any elections were swayed. State audits and independent studies have found voter fraud is very rare. A Reuters investigation published in July found that just 129 people had been prosecuted for noncitizen voting since a law criminalizing it was passed in 1996. The Justice Department [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"charged"] an additional 20 people this month. The Department of Homeland Security has obtained voter rolls from at least 47 of the 50 US states and is reviewing them to identify noncitizens who are registered, [USN:L6N45D0T4 TEXT:"Reuters reported"] on Thursday, citing an internal email. It remains unclear how many of those were redacted, public versions as opposed to a full accounting. The public versions often lack key personal identifying information such as partial Social Security numbers, dates of birth and driver's license numbers. DHS is using information from a commercial data broker to supplement the records, though it is not clear how much personally identifying information the department now possesses. Even if the Trump administration prevails in court in the case heard on Friday, it is not clear whether the DHS effort to create citizenship lists would have any impact on who is eligible to vote in November. Trump's executive order directed DHS to share the lists with state election officials at least 60 days before each federal election. That would have been September 4.

item.title: Pact with Saudi and Pakistan could expand to Muslim world, including Iran, says Turkish speaker
item.description: Similar to NATO's Article 5, the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Pact with Saudi and Pakistan could expand to Muslim world, including Iran, says Turkish speaker

Similar to NATO's Article 5, the "Mecca Joint Defence Agreement" stipulates that an attack on one ally constitutes an attack on all.

Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan meets with Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York City, US, on Sep 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Turkish Foreign Ministry)

25 Sep 2026 06:08PM (Updated: 25 Sep 2026 06:13PM)
